founding.headline: 626 Labs builds exact-fit software.
founding.quote: I build tools, because care doesn't always scale.
paragraphs: 626 Labs builds exact-fit software. The founding argument is simple: it has never been easier to have the exact tools we need, and too much money has been going to too many companies for tools that only half fit. So we build and maintain our own, at a quality that rivals enterprise software, made to enhance the work people do instead of taking their jobs. We are here to make great products, even if only a handful of people need them. That's ok.

The line the lab was built on belongs to its founder: "I build tools, because care doesn't always scale." It is translation: take the care a person already has and build it into something that keeps working after their attention has to move on.

We hold that use converts skeptics. Not a demo, not a number, not a story: the tool working in someone's hands. The data in our tools is gathered, not assumed. The bar is a well-put-together piece of technology, and the bar is enterprise-grade. The edge of the portfolio is two words: play nice.

So the lab builds for inheritors it has not met. 626 is a phone exchange: the first three digits of the founder's parents' old phone number, digits that stood for years on unpainted buildings as he passed, leaving the neighborhood for school. The pattern has run once before: his father's sound and light company, Stage Productions, is carried on today by each of his siblings. The seven kids from his house will inherit 626 Labs the same way. Even one more is a win.

labRuns.lead: Every project above lives inside a purpose-built agent OS — private, not yet open source. The plugins are the lessons it taught us.

caption: The 626 Labs Dashboard is a private agent OS — Operation Center, decisions log, Architect AI, and Scanner / Voice / Whiteboard inputs — running as one surface across every active project. It watches the work, logs the decisions, and keeps the threads connected when we context-switch between a hotel app, a theater tool, and a plugin release in the same afternoon.
The Dashboard itself isn't open source. The Vibe plugins are — they're the lessons the Dashboard taught us, refactored so any builder on Claude Code gets the same tailwind.

products.title: Celestia 3
products.description: An AI technomancer that reads the actual sky. The Swiss Ephemeris engine was rebuilt to astronomical precision — not the second-rate math most astrology apps ship — so every chart is observatory-accurate. Converse with the Athanor, an AI oracle grounded in your real natal chart, across the Natal Compass, Aura Cam, Arithmancy, Tarot, Rituals, Chronos forecasts, Celebrity Match, Synastry, and the Grimoire. The full tarot library is live and editorially reviewed card by card, a free birth-chart calculator needs no login, and a /learn library of placement readings keeps growing toward full coverage. Synastry readings now save to your Grimoire instead of re-running the AI every time you revisit a past match.

products.title: Conundrum by Este
products.description: The 626 Labs merch shop — streetwear-grade prints designed by an AI pipeline and sold print-on-demand on Etsy. Gemini generates the art (always textless — type is composited after, so the lettering is real), a QA pass filters the AI slop, classical CV cuts the backgrounds, and one base artwork fans out into a full variant matrix before anything ships. Human approval gates every publish. Socks, joggers, totes, hats.

products.title: Vibe Cartographer
products.tagline: Find your direction no matter where you start.
products.description: From a raw idea, eight commands walk you to a shipped app: onboard, scope, PRD, spec, checklist, build, iterate, reflect. Each step reads what the last one wrote, so the plan compounds instead of drifting. From anything else, /take runs the list you already have: a backlog, a findings report, someone else's plan, or the work it finds in the repo itself. It plans what needs planning and runs the rest the way you would, overnight if you say so, with nothing pushed until you review. {{fact:cmd_vibe-cartographer_word}} slash commands, one builder profile that remembers you.

products.title: Vibe Iterate
products.description: What to build next, after the app ships. Pick a banner mode — feature-add, competitive, ux-polish, bug-bash — and it scans competitors, framework releases, and your own feedback, scores the candidates, and ships one regression-aware PR. Sidecars (:radar, :spy, :scan-releases, :rate, :ship, :upgrade) cover the in-between. Every iteration logs to an Atlas — what won, what didn't, and why — so the next call starts where the last one ended.

products.title: Vibe Insights
products.description: The deep retrospective for your Claude Code work — the verbose /insights over your full history and every machine you code on. Coverage, where-was-I recall, token/cost with the cache reveal, trends, how-you-work, ranked open threads, decisions, languages, per-session friction, and a synthesized read of how you actually work. Personal by default, no telemetry; keep any source or repo local-only.

products.title: Vibe Keystone
products.tagline: Map the repo before the agent starts.
products.description: The bootstrap pass for any repo. Inventories the tech stack, side-tools, and bot workflows, then drafts a CLAUDE.md so the next agent lands oriented instead of blind. Interviews you for what it can't infer — org, decision surface, voice rules, persona — so the file reflects your conventions, not boilerplate. The keystone is the load-bearing file every later agent decision rests on; set it once and let it carry.

products.title: Vibe Doc
products.description: Point it at your codebase and it finds the docs you're missing — ADRs, runbooks, threat models, specs — then writes them from what's actually in the repo. Scans for gaps, scores deployment readiness, and drafts the pieces you keep meaning to write, asking you only for the calls a machine shouldn't make. A CI check keeps the set honest as the code moves.

products.title: Vibe Test
products.tagline: Put your code to the test before somebody else does.
products.description: Reads your vibe-coded app, classifies maturity tier and deployment risk, then generates the tests that actually matter — the ones tied to user impact, the release, the environment, not the ones that pad a number. Covers what the agent skipped when you're unsure what to test, and calls the broken harness fast: a vitest config silently reporting 0%, a green bar that's lying. Catches it before it sends you down the wrong road.

products.title: Vibe Thesis
products.description: Scaffolds thesis-shaped projects — dissertation, thesis, position essay — starting from sources you defend, challenge, or endorse, not a cold prompt. Runs a voice synthesis pass so it reads in your voice, not an LLM's, and guards the self-review tell: a model over-naming its own subject in the same flat cadence. Renders to PDF, HTML, and a lay version you can read in a sitting or hand to an agent. Built on ThesisStudio.

products.title: Thesis Engine
products.tagline: Surface topics. Gather sources. Seed the thesis.
products.description: Research feeder for Vibe Thesis. Surfaces cutting-edge topics in any domain, then gathers primary sources, opposing positions, and methodological precedents — the opposing ones on purpose, so you argue fair and mine the other side for merit. Emits a run folder that drops into ThesisStudio, research done and structured. Optional stage three turns a topic into a Smart Brevity blog draft for ideas that aren't thesis-sized.

products.title: Sanduhr für Claude
products.description: Native desktop widget that shows how fast you're burning through your Claude.ai usage, so you can pace yourself instead of finding out you're out of tokens at 11pm. Burn-rate projection, pace markers, sparkline trends, five hand-tuned glass themes — and per-model weekly meters that track your Claude Fable 5 allowance automatically: when Anthropic adds a limit for a new model, its bar just appears, no update needed. The Claude Usage tab turns your local Claude Code logs into a dashboard — sessions stacked by project with agent roll-up, weekly trends, a clickable usage calendar, sent/received splits, CSV export — with an opt-in local vault so your history outlives Claude Code's 30-day log cleanup. Threshold alerts chime softly when a pool crosses your line. Free on the Microsoft Store with real Win11 Mica glass, Apple-notarized for Mac with Sparkle auto-updates, single-file Python for everyone else. No telemetry — the only network call is to claude.ai with your own cookie.
products.meta: Free on MS Store · Mac + Win native

products.title: Vibe Sec
products.description: The security gaps AI prototyping leaves behind are predictable — leaked secrets, sketchy auth, missing input validation, stale dependencies. Vibe Sec audits across twelve concerns, calibrated to where your app actually runs, then writes the fix and routes it by confidence so nothing destructive lands on its own. Fast secret and dependency scans, a STRIDE threat model, and a CI gate that fails the build before the gap ships.

products.title: Vibe Taker
products.description: Move a feature between repos without copy-paste archaeology — no more pointing an agent at an old folder to "go get that." Captures it as a portable bundle: architecture, contract, gotchas, and the prompts that built it — so the destination repo continues your original process instead of pasting dead code, adapted to its stack. For a signature feature you want everywhere, or a prototype you lift into the next build. Local-only.

products.title: Vibe Wrap
products.tagline: Sessions wrap themselves when the trail is already there.
products.description: End-of-session wrap-up that reads the breadcrumb trail your toolkit already left instead of cold-reconstructing from git log. Multi-repo aware — it surfaces what shipped across every repo you touched, what's still uncommitted, and what's still unpushed, then gates commit and push on the current repo only. The result is a written record you can read, share, or paste into a status update.

products.title: Vibe Walk
products.description: vibe-walk reads your app, names the aha moment, and builds a spotlight tour you own outright — Driver.js module, anchor codemod, six analytics events wired to track what actually lands. And it's honest about fit: if a tour won't help, it tells you before you build one.

products.title: Vibe Prompt
products.tagline: Close the prompt loop: scan, audit, eval, grade, fix.
products.description: vibe-prompt inventories every prompt your site uses, then audits each one across five structural dimensions — catching the 13 flagged failure patterns (F1–F13) that range from missing persona to absent output constraints. A calibrated LLM judge runs behavioral eval so you catch regressions, not just structural smells. Confidence-routed fixes apply changes only where the signal is clear; uncertain ones surface for your call. Handoff to vibe-sec is built in for prompts that touch sensitive surfaces.

products.title: Vibe Lingual
products.tagline: Localize your app's UI without corrupting its logic.
products.description: vibe-lingual is the i18n-retrofit layer for vibe-coded apps. It scans every user-facing string by kind — JSX text, placeholder, aria-label, title, alt, toast, locale-sensitive date — audits the stack for the gotchas that bite localization retrofits, then runs a confidence-routed extract → wire → translate → guard loop that mutates only with per-file backups and idempotent re-runs. Deep on next-intl + App Router, with a real adapter seam that reports an honest not-yet-implemented for the rest instead of mishandling them. Validated by localizing most of Celestia3 — 720 strings across ~67 components.

products.title: Vibe Access
products.tagline: Give agents pipelines into your app.
products.description: vibe-access scans your routes and auth model, maps every callable surface into a schema-versioned agent-access.json manifest with dev and prod-safe tiers, scaffolds the affordances your app is missing behind hard env gates, then proves the layer with a cold-agent verify that exercises every affordance before anything counts as done. Seed, reset, and capture can never be tagged prod-safe: a refusal, not a warning. Adapters for Firebase Cloud Functions and Streamlit, with a real adapter seam that reports an honest not-yet-implemented for the rest. Validated against WeSeeYouAtTheMovies: 84 routes scanned, 85 affordances, verify 76/85.

products.title: Vibe Glow
products.tagline: Take an app from working to wanted.
products.description: vibe-glow runs a repeatable, gated UI and QOL beautification campaign, app-wide with an invented design language or scoped to one area with a goal in your own words. Four stages (identity, audit, wave, reveal) each run only on your yes: a measuring stick first, then a skeptic-verified findings register, then fix batches re-reviewed until clean, then the flagship release. Review agents run on Opus, per-app invariants like user theming outrank findings, and evidence adapters cover WinUI (PowerShell capture) and web (Playwright).

products.title: Vibe Runbook
products.tagline: A runbook that checks itself against the running system.
products.description: A runbook says do X and you will see W. Nothing checks whether that is still true. vibe-runbook writes one by inspecting your app, then verifies its claims against a running system. It scans a runbook and classifies every claim by shape, walks the machine-checkable ones against an environment you name with six verdicts (PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED, SPENDS, HUMAN, QUESTION), and offers the fix when a pin has gone stale. Read-only, never spends, and honest about what it could not check: every report states how many of the enumerated claims it actually checked.

products.title: Vibe Recall
products.tagline: Have you already built this? Check your own repos first.
products.description: vibe-recall indexes your own git repos and surfaces prior art while you spec the next feature. It builds a shallow card per repo (symbol names, dependency names, entrypoint paths, short claim strings, never a file body), ranks those cards against a phrase or spec file with scoring that explains itself, and hands real hits to a brief that re-reads the source live at current HEAD before claiming anything. Tenant walls you configure are refusals, not preferences. Zero hits is a real answer.

products.description: Adds 'Convert to PNG' and 'Copy as PNG' to the File Explorer right-click menu — decodes .webp / .avif / .heic / .bmp / .tif / .gif locally, no network round trip. C++/WinRT shell extension plus a .NET 9 AOT engine, seven bundled decoders, 85 tests green. Idea to Microsoft Store in 24 hours, built with Vibe Cartographer.

sections.title: Right Click
sections.dek: Convert images to PNG from the right-click menu. No network calls, no detours. Adds Convert to PNG and Copy as PNG to the File Explorer context menu, so the round-trip through an online converter stops happening.

paragraphs: Some images just don't download and paste. You save a .webp from the web, try to drop it into Teams or Figma, and the app rejects it. You save a .heic from your phone, and your image editor refuses to open it.
The workaround is always the same: find an online converter, upload the file, download a PNG, move it to where you actually needed it.

blocks.text: Right Click PNG replaces that detour with a right-click.

sections.heading: Two verbs where you already are

paragraphs: Right-click any .webp, .avif, .heic, .heif, .jpg, .jpeg, .bmp, .tif, .tiff or .gif in File Explorer. No separate app to open.

items.title: Convert to PNG
items.body: Saves a PNG next to the original, same base name, new extension.

items.title: Copy as PNG
items.body: Sends PNG bytes to the clipboard, ready to paste into Teams, Slack, Discord, Figma, Photoshop, Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, OneNote, Paint or Snipping Tool. Works on a .png too, for the paste without opening the file.

items.title: The whole selection at once
items.body: Multi-select files and the right-click action runs against the whole selection in one shot, with a single summary toast when the batch completes.

items.title: Two toggles, one window
items.body: A branded settings window with a dark title bar, opened from the Start menu or from the right-click menu itself. Confirm-before-overwrite lives here. Changes apply on the next right-click, no reboot.

items.title: JPEG when you need it
items.body: Convert to JPEG and Copy as JPEG are both there, hidden behind a settings toggle for anyone who needs them.

sections.heading: Idea to Microsoft Store in 24 hours

paragraphs: Built end to end with Vibe Cartographer, from the first scoping question to a signed MSIX approved on the Store. Shipped 2026-04-22.

items.title: The shell extension
items.body: A Win32 COM server that File Explorer hosts directly, the same way it hosts Windows' own right-click verbs. It stays minimal on purpose: read the selection, read settings, launch the engine, show the toast.

items.title: The engine
items.body: A standalone converter, called once per invocation. No runtime warm-up. Decoding runs on bundled libwebp, libavif, libheif, libspng and libjpeg-turbo; BMP, GIF and TIFF are read by hand-rolled C#.

items.title: One package
items.body: Signs and packages both, and registers the COM classes and file-type associations. The Store install auto-updates and uninstalls cleanly.

paragraphs: The engine and the shell extension are split across a process boundary on purpose. Explorer loads the extension as a DLL, so a decoder that crashes on a malformed file takes down a short-lived engine process, never Explorer. The extension sees a non-zero exit code and shows an error toast.
Disconnect, and it all still works.

rows.label: No network
rows.body: No network calls of any kind. No update checks, no phone-home. The engine's P/Invoke bindings carry no HTTP, because there's no HTTP. Read the source and check.

rows.label: No telemetry
rows.body: No telemetry, no crash reports, no analytics. No account, no sign-in, no cloud sync. Install it, use it, that's the whole surface.

rows.label: Original never touched
rows.body: The original file is never modified, moved or deleted. Convert writes a new file beside it.

rows.label: Color kept
rows.body: ICC color profiles are preserved when the source has one. No profile in, no profile out.

rows.label: Rotation kept
rows.body: EXIF orientation is baked into the pixel data before the metadata is stripped, so rotated photos stay rotated.

products.title: SnapSnip
products.description: Renames every Snipping Tool capture after the app and window it came from: Win+Shift+S or Print Screen, and “Screenshot 2026-04-29 142301.png” becomes “Outlook — Q3 forecast — 2026-04-29 142301.png”, with the same context embedded as XMP. Window titles are redacted on your machine first (Strict / Balanced / Permissive, per-app overrides, profiles). v0.3 adds a Library with Collections, and a Review clean-up for exact copies, near copies and blurry photos that never deletes and can be undone run by run. No network calls.

products.title: RORORO
products.description: Multi-launcher for Windows — run multiple Roblox clients side by side, each signed in as a different saved account. Native .NET 10 / WPF, DPAPI-encrypted account vault tied to your Windows user, embedded WebView2 login so your password never touches the app process. System-tray UX with state-coloured ring, per-game launch routing, Velopack auto-update. A hardened plugin host — sideload-only, https-only installs, named-pipe IPC with per-capability consent — with an in-app marketplace to browse, install, and update the Ur family in one click. Watches every client's memory and offers a one-click Recycle before a memory leak takes the window down, alongside stray-process cleanup, tray-residence recovery, Limited-account detection, idle-awareness that warns before Roblox's AFK kick, and a signed roblox-compat feed published on every release. Alerts reach your desktop, a Discord webhook, or your phone through Pushover or ntfy — with an every-two-hours all-good mark while your accounts run — and a History tab keeps score: most alts at once, total hours, per-alt login streaks. Trust-aware Squad Launch lands a group in the same server together, streamer mode swaps in fake names and avatars when you're live, and four themes plus a builder let you tune the app and share the result as a file. Mac-native sibling, and a three-plugin family: Ur Task (portable, window-aware macros), Ur OCR (screen triggers that fire keybinds or Ur Task macros), and Ur AFK (one-tap keep-alive). Speaks six languages — French, German, Russian, Portuguese, Polish, Spanish — following your Windows language or pinned in Settings. Free on the Microsoft Store. Independent third-party tool — not affiliated with Roblox Corporation.

products.title: 626 Mod Launcher
products.description: A reversible, atomic mod toggler for PC games — Bethesda, Unreal, FromSoft, BepInEx, Stardew SMAPI, and more. Disabling a mod moves its files to a holding folder instead of deleting them, so every toggle is reversible and every state change writes atomically — lose power mid-toggle and your library survives. Drag a zip onto the window and it identifies the mod, fills in the real name, author, and source link, then installs it where the loader actually expects. Free on the Microsoft Store as the signed sealed-core build (no SmartScreen warning); the GitHub build adds Nexus integration, and 626 Mod Launcher is officially accepted by Nexus Mods. No ads, no telemetry, no account.

products.title: 626 POD Pipeline
products.tagline: Concept to live Etsy listing — nine stages, one human gate.
products.description: The open-source engine behind Conundrum by Este: a Python script library that takes a concept to a live Etsy listing in nine stages. Gemini art generation, an AI-slop QA gate, classical-CV background removal, PIL type compositing, and a variant matrix that fans one artwork into a full product line before Printify upload and Etsy publish. No app server, no build step, a JSON-backed catalog — and a human go gates every publish.

products.title: 626Labs Agentic Sales Connector
products.tagline: Read-focused eyes on your Etsy shop, for any AI assistant.
products.description: A hosted MCP connector that connects Claude — and any MCP client — to an Etsy seller's shop data through Etsy's official Open API v3. Shop snapshots, listing performance, orders, reviews, and day-over-day movers. Etsy's API reports lifetime counters only, so the connector takes a daily snapshot server-side and computes the difference — movement that does not otherwise exist as data — on a cloud schedule, so your computer does not need to be on. Sign-in happens only on etsy.com's own consent screen, on four read scopes; tokens are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM, your history exports to CSV anytime, and it purges 30 days after you disconnect. Every answer is stamped with how fresh it is and where it came from; an unreadable number comes back as unknown, never as zero. No scraping — the official API plus optional seller-provided CSV imports, labeled by source. Zero tools modify your Etsy shop. In private testing with Conundrum by Este.

sections.heading: Your shop data, where your assistant already is

paragraphs: The connector links Claude — and any other MCP client — to an Etsy seller's shop data through Etsy's official Open API v3. You ask the questions in the assistant you already use; it reads the answers out of your shop.

Version 1 is read-focused, which is a narrower word than read-only and the accurate one. Seven of its nine tools only fetch and summarize. The other two write, but never to Etsy: one parses a CSV you exported yourself into the connector's own store, and one deletes everything the connector holds about your shop.

Etsy's API reports lifetime counters — total views, total favorites — so it cannot tell you what changed since yesterday. The connector takes a daily snapshot server-side and computes the difference, which is what makes movement exist as data at all. Because those snapshots run on a schedule in the cloud, your computer does not need to be on.

items.title: Shop snapshots
items.body: The state of the shop at a point in time — the baseline everything else is measured against.

items.title: Listing performance

items.title: Orders

items.title: Reviews

items.title: Day-over-day movers
items.body: What changed since yesterday, computed from snapshot history rather than fetched — the trend line the API does not hand you directly.

blocks.label: Read-only, by construction

sections.heading: What it can reach, and what it can never do

paragraphs: A connector asking for access to a live storefront should be able to say precisely what it takes and where it puts it. This is that list.

rows.label: Credentials
rows.body: Sign-in happens only on etsy.com's own consent screen. You are never asked to enter your Etsy credentials anywhere else — not in the connector, not on this site, not in your assistant.

rows.label: Scopes
rows.body: Minimal, read-only, and named in full:

codes.desc: read your shop profile and stats
read reviews left on your shop

rows.codesNote: Every one ends in _r. There is no write scope in the set, so the grant itself is what makes the read-only promise, not just the code.

rows.label: Your data, portable
rows.body: Full CSV export, anytime. What the connector has collected is yours to take out in a format that opens in anything.

rows.label: Your data, deletable
rows.body: Immediate on request. And automatic on disconnect, in two speeds: access tokens are destroyed right away, while stored history keeps a 30-day grace period so reconnecting does not cost you your snapshots. After that it purges whether you ask or not.

rows.label: Honest numbers
rows.body: Every answer carries a timestamp and a source, so you always know whether you are reading a live pull, a cached value, or something derived from snapshots. A number that cannot be read comes back as unknown, with a reason — never as a zero. If the connection breaks, the tools say so and hand back a reconnect link instead of serving stale figures.

rows.label: No scraping
rows.body: Data comes from the official API, plus optional CSV imports you provide yourself. Every figure is labeled by source, so API-derived and seller-supplied numbers never get quietly averaged together.

paragraphs: Currently in private testing with our own shop, Conundrum by Este. Public availability is planned after maturation and review through Etsy's Commercial Access and Anthropic's Connectors Directory.

products: We See You at the Movies

paragraphs: 626 Labs builds modern tools for practices that have been running on spreadsheets, paper, and inherited habits for decades — or, in the case of astrology, a few thousand years. The brief is simple: look at a field that everyone assumes is "fine the way it is," and ship the version it should have had all along.

The proof case is Celestia 3. AI joined with tarot, numerology, and astrology in one surface. Partway through the build, we discovered the default Swiss Ephemeris engine drifted at the second-precision level. We didn't ship around it. We repaired the engine ourselves and met the NASA-grade bar. The point isn't the math — it's the posture. When the bar moves mid-build, we move with it.

That posture is what pulled us into the old empires — legacy operations, safety inspections, hotels, cinema exhibition. Off-the-shelf vendors build for the brochure. We build operator-first — the domain expert in the loop, the AI coder on the keyboard — and ship the tool the shift manager actually needed.

The Vibe plugins — {{fact:live_plugin_names}} — are the other half of the work. Vibe coding is the fastest way to turn an idea into running software right now. It's also the easiest way to end up with something that can't survive production. The plugins close that gap: planning, docs, tests, security, all built so a vibe-coded afternoon holds up in front of real users.
We See You at the Movies is the gaming wedge. Trivia and head-to-head card battles are warm-ups for bigger things on deck.

Every 626 Labs app is built like it might be seen by a thousand pairs of eyes, even when it may only ever be seen by one. That's the standard. I've deployed more apps to production than I ever imagined, and the bar keeps going up. Read the whole story.
